name: Win back churned customers from Stripe and HubSpot with Claude-written emails

parameters.content:
## Win back churned customers from Stripe and HubSpot with Claude-written emails

**Who's it for**
SaaS growth teams that never contact churned accounts again, even when the reason they left is fixed.

**How it works**
Trigger: Weekly scan of churned accounts against triggers; release-notes webhook or a manual trigger when a feature ships; seasonal calendar for seasonal businesses.
1. Build the churned segment
2. Classify the reason
3. Match triggers to segments
4. Draft the message
5. Approve high-value sends
6. Send and route replies
7. Track reactivation
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items instead of guessing, and the write-back waits for an approval in Slack or Gmail.

**How to set up**
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials to each service node.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

**Requirements**
An Anthropic API key for the Claude nodes, plus Stripe / Chargebee + HubSpot, Gmail / Customer.io (or their equivalents — the nodes are standard and easy to swap).

**How to customize the workflow**
Define the win-back triggers and the offer rules in the Config node; send through Customer.io or Gmail. Keep the guardrail: Excluded segments (business closed, requested no contact, poor fit) never receive win-back messages.

Full blueprint with trigger, steps, guardrails and where the standard version stops: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/customer-win-back-automation/

## Customer Win-Back Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Weekly scan of churned accounts against triggers; release-notes webhook or a manual trigger when a feature ships; seasonal calendar for seasonal businesses.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Excluded segments (business closed, requested no contact, poor fit) never receive win-back messages.
   - One win-back message per account per quarter unless they reply.
   - Offers come only from the approved set; the agent picks, it never invents a discount.
   - High-value accounts require owner approval before sending.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/customer-win-back-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $197/month · custom $2,000–3,500 one-time

## Steps

1. Schedule Trigger (weekly)
2. HTTP Request: Build the churned segment
3. Text Classifier: Classify the reason
4. Code: Match triggers to segments
5. AI Agent: Draft the message
6. Wait: Approve high-value sends
7. Gmail: Send and route replies
8. HubSpot: Track reactivation

Every AI step is followed by "Needs a person?"; the write-back waits for "Approved?" where the blueprint has an approval step.

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

- CRM and exit-survey text
- Release notes / product changelog

Cancelled and lapsed accounts from billing and CRM with tenure, last plan, revenue, cancellation reason and any exit-survey text.

nodes.name: Text Classifier: Classify the reason
nodes.notes:
Classify the reason

Exit reasons normalised into categories — price, missing feature, poor fit, switched to competitor, business closed, unresponsive — from the survey text and support history.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Classify the reason
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Code: Match triggers to segments
nodes.notes:
Match triggers to segments

Rules: missing-feature churn waits for that feature to ship; price churn waits for a plan change or an annual-discount window; seasonal churn waits for the season; poor-fit and closed-business are excluded.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft the message" step of the Customer Win-Back Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: A short, specific message referencing the reason they gave and the thing that changed, with one approved offer from the finance-owned set, in the account owner's voice.

Rules:
- Excluded segments (business closed, requested no contact, poor fit) never receive win-back messages.
- One win-back message per account per quarter unless they reply.
- Offers come only from the approved set; the agent picks, it never invents a discount.
- High-value accounts require owner approval before sending.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
